questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the crossing guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in a school zone.

questions.question: From top to bottom, traffic lights are arranged in this order:

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is always on top and green is on the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is always on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: You can turn right on red if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and check for traffic and pedestrians.
Are facing a red arrow.
Are in the left lane.
Slow down first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and check for traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You can turn right at a red light unless there is a sign that says you cannot. You must stop completely first and let pedestrians and other traffic go. Check that it is safe before turning.

questions.question: What can you do from a center turn lane?

options.text: You can make left turns.
You can make U-turns.
You can pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: A center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it to pass other cars or to drive straight through.

questions.question: When the traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Get ready to stop for the red light if you can do so safely.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Move out of their way.
Look at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up as they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.explanation: Try to stay away from an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact with them. Speeding up may make them even angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must:

options.text: Stop five feet away from the bus.
Stop only if you can see children are getting on or off.
Stop and stay stopped until it is safe to go.
Stop and stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop at least 10 feet away. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing, the arm is pulled back, and children have crossed safely. This rule applies whether you are behind the bus, facing it, or at an intersection with it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them so they will not cross against the light again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and other cars in the intersection, even if you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers and carefully leave the road. Park where other drivers can see you clearly. Lift your hood to show your car is broken down.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you plan to change direction.

questions.question: If your blood alcohol level is 0.04 percent, what is true?

options.text: You are two to seven times more likely to crash than someone who has not drunk any alcohol.
You are above the legal limit but still safe to drive.
You can be sure you will drive safely.
You should drink plenty of coffee before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are two to seven times more likely to crash than someone who has not drunk any alcohol.
questions.explanation: No amount of alcohol is safe before driving. At 0.04 percent blood alcohol, which is below the legal limit for adults 21 and older, you are two to seven times more likely to crash than someone with no alcohol in their system.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the road ahead for long periods of time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road ahead for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long without looking around. You stop scanning ahead, behind, and to the sides of your vehicle. This makes you likely to crash into traffic that is slowing or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder for an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or poor weather.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: If a truck swings left before turning right, what is dangerous to do?

options.text: Try to squeeze between the truck and the curb to turn right.
Apply your brakes until the truck finishes turning.
Break the four-second following distance rule.
Honk your horn at the truck driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to squeeze between the truck and the curb to turn right.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need to swing wide to turn. A truck swinging left may actually be turning right. Do not try to pass a turning truck. Truck drivers cannot see vehicles squeezed between them and the curb.

questions.question: What causes most traffic deaths in work zones?

options.text: Tire blowouts.
Hydroplaning from water on the road.
Loss of steering control from wet paint.
Carelessness and speeding.

questions.explanation: Carelessness and speeding are the main causes of traffic deaths in work zones.
